title: Keystone latency SLI rollup and region whitelist failover playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: build a low-cardinality rollup ("keystone") of token-level latency SLIs that powers a compact regional failover decision surface and an operational playbook for region whitelisting during partial outages. Motivation came from recent incidents where high per-token tail latency in a single region caused churny circuit states and noisy dashboards. Current token-level pipelines are high fidelity but too high-cardinality for fast routing decisions and on-call consumption. This ticket scopes: (1) definition of the keystone rollup metric, (2) instrumentation changes to export the rollup alongside existing token SLIs, (3) Grafana dashboard panels and a live decision annotator that surfaces why a region was placed on the whitelist/blacklist, and (4) an on-call playbook describing manual and automated run paths for region whitelist failover.
acceptance_criteria: Keystone rollup metric implemented and emitted on prod telemetry topic with stable schema
Keystone-based failover decision annotated in the operational dashboard with links to related token SLI heatmaps
Grafana dashboard created with compact panels for region-level keystone, per-shard spillover, and recent circuit actions
Playbook published to Confluence and tested in the chaos playground with a simulated region degradation
Synthetic-run comparison shows keystone-based policy reduces noisy failovers by >= 40% versus baseline

notes: Trade-offs: lower-cardinality rollup aids operator speed but loses some failure mode fidelity. Mitigation: keep token-level SLI pipeline and expose a drilldown in the dashboard; add automated sampling when keystone crosses thresholds.
Operational recommendation: start with read-only 'whitelist candidate' annotations for two weeks before enabling automatic region move to blacklist.
